subject: Myth & Symbolism
subcategory: The World Tree and Cosmic Maps
title: Here Be Dragons
description: A 60-second lesson on Here Be Dragons.

hook.text: Old maps filled unknown regions with monsters. 'Here be dragons' warns sailors the world's edge is dangerous.

buildup.text: The Lenox Globe from 1510 is one of the few maps that literally says 'HC SVNT DRACONES'—here are dragons.

discovery.text: Sea monsters on maps weren't just decoration. They encoded real fears about waters no one had survived to describe.

twist.text: The phrase 'here be dragons' is mostly a modern myth. Very few actual maps used it—but we remember the idea.

climax.text: Blank spaces on maps terrified mapmakers. They filled the unknown with myth because empty space felt impossible.

quiz.question: Which globe actually contains the phrase 'Here be dragons' in Latin?
